transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I guess I came in because... it's mostly happening after my late shifts. I work at the family entertainment center out by the mall—the one with the laser tag and the arcade? You wouldn't believe how exhausting it is. Just last weekend, some kid threw a plastic prize cup right at my head, and the parents didn't even say anything. People are just so rude these days, you know? 

But anyway, after those late shifts, I’ll usually stop for food on the drive back. And then I just... keep going once I get home. Like, I’ll finish a full takeout meal, and then I'm into the chips, the sweets, just whatever’s in the apartment. My roommate left this weird spicy trail mix out on the counter once and I even ate all of that, which is funny because I usually hate spicy food. It gives me terrible heartburn. My dad gets bad heartburn too, actually, he has to take those little purple pills every morning... but yeah, afterward I just look around at the kitchen and I’m genuinely shocked by how much I actually ate.
When you find yourself eating all of that food after work, does it feel like you can’t stop or control yourself once you start?

Yeah, that's exactly it. Once I start on those nights, it’s like I’m watching myself from the outside, you know? I'll be in my head telling myself to just put the food away, but my hands just keep opening containers until everything is gone. 

Which is crazy because my roommate has this huge stack of those fancy glass Tupperware containers with the heavy snap lids. He got a whole set of them on clearance at Target. I was actually at Target on Tuesday trying to find some gel inserts for my work shoes. Standing on that arcade carpet for eight, sometimes ten hours straight just completely destroys my arches. And the carpet has this crazy neon geometric pattern—it's like straight out of 1994—and it literally makes you dizzy if you stare at it too long while you're walking around resetting the games. I told my manager we need to replace it, but he never listens to me. 

But um... yeah, I just keep opening those lids and wrappers, and I can't seem to make myself stop until the food is just gone.
Does this eating behavior cause you distress or interfere with your daily life in any way?

Well, yeah, it does bother me a lot. I mean, I'm still showing up for work and everything, but it's getting in the way. Like, the guys at work always want to go to Denny's after our shift. We used to go all the time, and Joey—he's the guy who runs the go-karts—he always orders this massive Grand Slam breakfast thing, even at like 2 AM. I don't know how he eats all that grease right before bed. His uniform always smells like fry oil, actually. We have to wear these awful polyester polo shirts that just trap every single scent. I tried washing mine with that new sports detergent, the one in the blue bottle? It's supposed to get rid of odors, but it just made my shirt smell like fake mountain air mixed with stale popcorn. 

But anyway, I've started dodging those Denny's trips with them. I just make up excuses because I know I need to get home to... well, do my own thing. And then my whole morning is ruined. Instead of sleeping in or going to the bank or whatever, I'm just planning my whole morning around trying to undo what I did the night before. I'm just so exhausted. I was supposed to take my car in for an oil change three weeks ago, but I just haven't had the energy. The little sticker on the windshield is driving me crazy, though. It's starting to peel at the corners.
After these episodes of eating a lot of food, do you ever try to make up for it by making yourself vomit, using laxatives, or doing extra exercise?

Yeah... I do. Like, sometimes after I get home and eat way too much of that takeout or all those snacks, I'll go straight into the bathroom and just... make myself throw up. I just do it so the food won't sit in me and turn into weight, you know? 

But honestly, spending that much time in our bathroom lately has been driving me crazy because the plumbing in our building is just terrible. The toilet runs constantly. My roommate tried to fix it himself by bending that little metal arm inside the tank, but he just made it worse. He thinks he's so handy because he watches those DIY home renovation shows on HGTV. The ones where they buy a rundown barn and turn it into a modern farmhouse? My mom loves those shows. She actually painted her kitchen cabinets white last summer because of one of those episodes, but she didn't sand them first, so now the paint is chipping off right around the handles. It looks awful, especially near the sink where she washes dishes. She uses this lemon-scented soap that smells exactly like the floor cleaner we use at the arcade. 

But um... yeah, so I just go in there and make myself sick so I don't gain weight from it all.
